votes.question: On Passage — National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This bill authorizes fiscal year 2027 military programs, troop levels, and related Energy Department national-security work. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: The fiscal year 2027 defense bill sets military policy, troop levels, and related Energy Department security programs. This vote would have sent that bill back to the Armed Services Committee with no rewrite attached. A Yea would have pulled it off the floor; a Nay left it up for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have required the Defense Secretary to report options for cutting the department's civilian workforce by 200,000. A Yea would have added that report. A Nay voted not to add it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to the fiscal year 2027 defense bill would ban automated speed-enforcement cameras on military bases. A Yea adds that ban to the bill. A Nay leaves the bill without it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) would have let the Secretary approve any eligible investor and cleared investment professional who meets the program's requirements to assess investment opportunities matching the department's needs, with no cap on participants, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment codifies protections and responsibilities for chaplains and subjects such protections to prosecution under the Uniform Code of Military Justice.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to authorize the Secretary of Defense to establish a school choice pilot program for members of the Armed Forces.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment prohibits male participation in female sports at Department of Defense Education Activity schools.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment prohibits gender-related medical care under TRICARE and prevents TRICARE from covering certain gender-related medical procedures and treatments.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) would have codified Executive Order 14183, which requires all personnel to serve in accordance with their biological sex, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment establishes a presumption of approval for qualified Department of Defense servicemembers and civilian employees seeking authorization from their facility commander to carry personal firearms on military installations.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “An amendment numbered 15 printed in Part A of House Report 119-755 to prohibit funds for Ukraine Security Assistance except for U.S. embassy security in Ukraine.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit the Department of Defense from using taxpayer funds to cover the costs of foreign military personnel participating in bilateral or multilateral military exercises conducted with the United States unless the Secretary of Defense waives the prohibition when necessary to support a U.S. national security interest.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to preempt state and local laws that impose requirements different from federal standards on certain defense-related recycling, disposal, and materials recovery activities.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) would have required a study of ways federal authority could preempt or otherwise mitigate state actions affecting domestic refining capacity for national defense, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) requires the continued operation of the Santa Ynez Pipeline System, which transports domestically produced crude oil to refineries that supply Department of Defense installations, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) would have barred courts from issuing injunctions that impair military readiness, military fuel supply, or defense-related logistical support, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment strikes section 518, relating to the pilot program on modernization of drug testing using voice-based risk assessment technology to identify servicemembers for drug testing.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to strike section 524, which removes the existing statutory limit on the number of cadets who may receive alternative service obligations to pursue professional athletic careers, thereby preserving the current cap.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to strike section 521 and replace it with a prohibition on foreign nationals attending the United States Military Academies.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to strike section 1213, relating to the deadline for the Afghanistan War Commission's final report, and maintain the current statutory reporting deadline.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Take Care of America’s Veterans Act (H R 9237)
votes.bill_title: Take Care of America’s Veterans Act
votes.plain_language: H.R. 9237 (Take Care of America’s Veterans Act) addresses veterans’ benefits, health care, counseling, Department of Veterans Affairs personnel, VA infrastructure, and the Veterans Community Care Program. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — To name the Department of Veterans Affairs multispecialty clinic in Marietta, Georgia, as the “Colonel Michael H. Boyce Department of Veterans Affairs Multispecialty Clinic” (H R 5362)
votes.bill_title: To name the Department of Veterans Affairs multispecialty clinic in Marietta, Georgia, as the "Colonel Michael H. Boyce Department of Veterans Affairs Multispecialty Clinic".
votes.plain_language: This bill designates the multispecialty clinic of the Department of Veterans Affairs in Marietta, Georgia, as the Colonel Michael H. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes (H R 9238)
votes.bill_title: To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This bill extends the authorities of Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act until July 2, 2026. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act (H R 6047)
votes.bill_title: Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill expands specified benefits programs for veterans and their survivors and establishes a supplemental monthly allowance for certain disabled veterans. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.bill_title: Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act
votes.plain_language: This bill prohibits the Department of Veterans Affairs from transmitting certain information to the National Instant Criminal Background Check System utilized by licensed importers or dealers of firearms. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act (H R 1041)
votes.bill_title: Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act
votes.plain_language: H.R. 1041 (Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act) prohibits the Department of Veterans Affairs from transmitting certain information to the National Instant Criminal Background Check System utilized by licensed importers or dealers of firearms. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Fiscal Year 2025 Veterans Affairs Major Medical Facility Authorization Act (S 2393)
votes.bill_title: Fiscal Year 2025 Veterans Affairs Major Medical Facility Authorization Act
votes.plain_language: This bill authorizes the Department of Veterans Affairs to carry out a major medical facility project in St. Louis, Missouri, during FY2026. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes (S 4465)
votes.bill_title: A bill to amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
votes.plain_language: This bill extends the authorities of Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act until June 12, 2026. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Fallen Servicemembers Religious Heritage Restoration Act (S 1318)
votes.bill_title: Fallen Servicemembers Religious Heritage Restoration Act
votes.plain_language: This bill carries the Foreign Intelligence Accountability Act and the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act as passed by the House; it reauthorizes Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act until April 30, 2029, with added protections related to Section 702, and bars Federal Reserve banks from issuing a central bank digital currency or offering accounts directly to individuals. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Ernest Peltz Accrued Veterans Benefits Act (H R 3123)
votes.bill_title: Ernest Peltz Accrued Veterans Benefits Act
votes.plain_language: This bill establishes procedures for the Department of Veterans Affairs to issue a pension that was due but unpaid at the time of a veteran’s death. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Veterans Readiness and Employment Improvement Act (H R 980)
votes.bill_title: Veterans Readiness and Employment Improvement Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill removes the requirement that educational and vocational counseling services provided by the Department of Veterans Affairs on campus at institutions of higher learning must be provided by VA counselors. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes (H R 5334)
votes.bill_title: Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 93)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes it, except for forces needed to defend against an imminent attack if the President follows the War Powers Resolution's time limits. A Yea agrees. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 89)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea agrees to that direction. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon (H CON RES 108)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon within seven days of the resolution's adoption. A Yea agrees to the concurrent resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Ukraine Support Act (H R 2913)
votes.bill_title: Ukraine Support Act
votes.plain_language: This bill addresses the war between Russia and Ukraine by (1) providing assistance to Ukraine and certain European countries, and (2) establishing penalties for Russia and certain foreign persons (individuals and entities). A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from Lebanon (H CON RES 84)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from Lebanon.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from Lebanon within seven days of the resolution's adoption. A Yea agrees to the concurrent resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 86)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran (H CON RES 75)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove the United States Armed Forces from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran or any part of its government or military no later than March 30, 2026, unless a declaration of war or authorization to use military force for such purpose has been enacted. votes.question: On Passage — To require the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status (H R 1689)
votes.bill_title: To require the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status.
votes.plain_language: This bill directs the Department of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status for 18 months beginning August 3, 2025. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from unauthorized hostilities in the Islamic Republic of Iran (H CON RES 38)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from unauthorized hostilities in the Islamic Republic of Iran.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Agree — Reaffirming Iran remains the largest state sponsor of terrorism (H RES 1099)
votes.bill_title: Reaffirming Iran remains the largest state sponsor of terrorism.
votes.plain_language: This resolution states that the House of Representatives declares it is the policy of the United States that Iran continues to be the largest state sponsor of terrorism. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports agreeing to it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — PROTECT Taiwan Act (H R 1531)
votes.bill_title: PROTECT Taiwan Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires certain federal entities to seek to exclude China from six international financial organizations if the President informs Congress that China's actions threaten Taiwan and pose a danger to U.S. interests. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.bill_title: To direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from Venezuela that have not been authorized by Congress.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
